source.locator: lines 32-35, definition of the represented provability formula

findings.finding: The prose defines OPrf as the formula representing the proof relation, but the immediately following definition of OProv quantifies the unrepresented relation symbol Prf instead.
findings.controlling_evidence: The preceding sentence and every later derivability condition use the object-language formula OPrf/OProv; the semantic relation Prf is not the formula that can occur inside arithmetic.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use OPrf in the OProv definition and add an adjacent OLTEINP-001 disclosure.

findings.finding: The formula drops the O prefix from the object-language provability predicate and writes Prov where the chapter has defined OProv.
findings.controlling_evidence: The preceding display, the Goedel fixed-point equivalence, and all formal proof lines use OProv for the representing formula.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore OProv and add an adjacent OLTEINP-002 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 89-94, explanation of the P2 substitution

findings.finding: The second P2 instantiation writes gn{G}, omitting the formula marker used by the displayed proof and every other occurrence gn{!G}.
findings.controlling_evidence: Line G2-6 is obtained by substituting the formula OProv(gn{!G}); the displayed formulas retain the marked metavariable throughout.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use gn{!G} and add an adjacent OLTEINP-003 disclosure.

findings.finding: The conclusion writes OCon[T] even though the theorem fixes the theory as Th{T} and uses that notation in the associated provability predicate.
findings.controlling_evidence: The chapter consistently parameterizes both OProv and OCon by the same theory object Th{T}; bare T is not the displayed theory macro here.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use OCon[Th{T}] and add an adjacent OLTEINP-004 disclosure.

source.locator: line 117, final inference in the proof of Loeb's theorem

findings.finding: The final inference cites L-8 and L-12 only, but L-12 yields Prov(D), whereas L-8 requires Prov(A); the bridge from Prov(D) to Prov(A) is L-7.
findings.controlling_evidence: L-7 states Prov(D) implies Prov(A), L-8 states Prov(A) implies A, and L-12 supplies Prov(D), so all three are required for the displayed conclusion A.
findings.required_translation_handling: Cite L-7, L-8, and L-12 and add an adjacent OLTEINP-005 disclosure.
